newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsica separatist alleges secret talks with Paris.
newsitem.headline: Corsica separatist alleges secret talks with Paris.

text.p: A Corsican separatist chief living in hiding said in an interview on Monday that his group had held secret talks with the French government and he named five officials he called its envoys.
Francois Santoni, head of the Cuncolta Naziunalista party, said one of the envoys was Maurice Gourdault-Montagne, a senior aide of Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
Juppe's office dismissed Santoni's statements as "grotesque lies by a terrorist".
Santoni's party is the legal side of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), "Historic Wing", the most hardline group on the Mediterranean island.

Santoni also alleged in an interview with the daily Est-Republicain newspaper that a night-time rally in January of 600 heavily-armed FLNC guerrillas was organised at the behest of the government, which wanted to show the French public the group was popular in Corsica and should be negotiated with.
The rally caused uproar in France, especially since no one one was arrested even though police seemed to know of it.

Juppe's office said in a statement: "The government has but one policy in Corsica: development of the island, which relies on re-asserting order and thus strictly applying the laws as the population desires."

French newspapers have long said the centre-right government has been in contact with the guerrillas in an effort to find a negotiated solution to end the 20-year low-level bombing campaign on the island.
The separatists maintained their bombings with an attack against the home of the mayor of the northern town of Bastia early on Monday.

The Bastia blast blew out the door of the apartment of Emile Zuccarelli, a former cabinet minister and opposition member of the National Assembly for the small Radical Socialist party. No one was hurt and Zuccarelli was not at home at the time.

The FLNC claimed responsibility for the attack in a statement to local media. It also said it was responsible for an attack in which the outside walls of an office of the paramilitary gendarmerie in Vescovato in northeastern Corsica were riddled with bullets on Monday.
